actions.body:
Research agenda management is critical to effective inquiry. A primary barrier is the sunk cost effect, defined as 'on an important human decision bias – the sunk cost effect. To address our research question, we use a
unique a' (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca). This bias causes agents to persist in failing paths. Furthermore, in planning tasks, 'or abandon it. We model planning tasks in which an agent with this type of bias tries
to reach a designated goa' (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da). To mitigate this, adaptive evaluation, often used in conservation, provides a better strategy for reallocating cognitive resources when epistemic returns diminish (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb). Abandonment is not failure; it is optimization of the research trajectory.
actions.lede: Intelligence often persists in unproductive research paths due to commitment bias; we examine formal criteria for abandoning such agendas based on diminishing epistemic returns.
